name: FAQ, myth and fact
description: Common myths shown struck through under a rotated stamp, each followed by the fact that corrects it. Always visible.

fields.name: title
fields.label: Title
fields.default: Six things your back wishes you would stop believing

fields.name: intro
fields.label: Intro
fields.default: We hear these in the treatment room every week. Here is what the research, and 14 years of sore backs, actually say.

itemFields.name: myth
itemFields.label: Myth
itemFields.default: Stretching before a run prevents injury.

itemFields.name: fact
itemFields.label: Fact
itemFields.default: A light warm-up protects you more. Save the long stretches for afterwards.

default.myth: If it hurts, rest until it stops.
default.fact: Gentle movement speeds up recovery for most back and joint pain. We show you which movements are safe from day one.

default.myth: You need a scan before treatment can start.
default.fact: Fewer than 1 in 20 people we see need imaging. A 45-minute assessment tells us more than most scans do.

default.myth: You need a referral from your GP.
default.fact: You can book with us directly. If you plan to claim on insurance, check whether your insurer asks for one.

default.myth: Physio means months of weekly visits.
default.fact: Most people need three to six sessions. You leave the first one with a plan you can follow at home.

default.myth: Good posture means sitting up straight all day.
default.fact: No single posture is the right one. Your next position is the healthiest, so change it every 30 minutes.
Studies have found no link. The pop is gas moving in the joint fluid, so crack away.
